issues.description: SealSaloon.stock field: The problem statement is inconsistent about whether the stock field is an instance-level final field or a static (class-level) final field. In problem_statement.md (line 70) the spec describes "a final Stock stock (meaning that it is read-only after construction)" and implies it should be initialized in the constructor (an instance final field). Later in the same problem statement (lines 77-81) the spec explicitly requires the stock attribute to be static and lists it among elements that "must be static" ("stock attribute: This is shared across all instances of the SealSaloon"). The solution implementation (SealSaloon.java, line 5) declares the field as static final. This contradiction (instance final vs static final) can confuse students about the correct declaration and initialization location for the stock field and whether methods that operate on it must be static.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the specification consistent: explicitly state in all relevant places that the SealSaloon.stock field is a static final Stock (shared across all instances). Update the earlier sentence that currently says "a final Stock stock (meaning that it is read-only after construction)" to read "a static final Stock stock (shared across all SealSaloon instances)" and remove any wording that implies instance initialization in the constructor. This aligns the textual spec with the UML note and the reference implementation and prevents student confusion about static vs instance declaration.

issues.description: SealSaloon.totalOrders field type: The UML in the problem statement defines SealSaloon.totalOrders as type int (problem_statement.md, UML line 28), but the solution implementation declares totalOrders as a long (solution SealSaloon.java, line 6: private long totalOrders = 0;). This mismatch between the specified UML type (int) and the reference implementation type (long) can confuse students about the expected field type and the return type of any getter for totalOrders.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type consistent across specification and implementation. Either: (A) change the UML/specification to declare totalOrders: long to match the reference implementation and the getter's return type; or (B) change the reference implementation to use int for totalOrders and adjust the getter accordingly. Prefer updating the UML/specification to 'long' if the intent is to allow large order counts, otherwise update the implementation to 'int' if the exercise intended 32-bit counts.
